name: Altiplano & Andes (La Paz · El Alto · Potosí · Salt Flats)

language.script_notes: Spanish signage with Aymara dominant around La Paz and Lake Titicaca and Quechua around Sucre, Potosí and Cochabamba; the Wiphala flag is everywhere.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Striped guardrails with a yellow outer stripe, common on dramatic mountain roads.
road_furniture.curb_style: Steep cobbled streets in La Paz; large stone paving in some towns.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Thick square lumber utility poles and thick unpainted sign posts; dolls hung on poles as anti-theft warnings in La Paz; the RN3 climbs steep, fog-prone mountains near the capital.

architecture.roof_style: Flat roofs of concrete and corrugated metal; rooftop chalet-style top floors on cholets.
architecture.wall_construction: Simple brick and cement construction at altitude, mostly unpainted; El Alto's neo-Andean cholets — flamboyant multi-storey buildings with geometric Andean-patterned facades, a shop below, an event hall above and an owner's chalet on the roof; whitewashed colonial buildings in Sucre.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Grey and orange brick, with dazzling multicolour cholets and blue-and-white painted telecom or party buildings.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Cholets in El Alto and La Paz; steep hillside barrios climbing La Paz's canyon; colonial plazas in Sucre and Potosí; adobe villages around Lake Titicaca; the Cerro Rico mining hill at Potosí.

nature.vegetation: A largely treeless landscape of ichu grass, thola bushes, quinoa fields and queñua shrubs; llamas and alpacas grazing on peat bogs; almost no trees at the highest altitudes.
nature.terrain: The Altiplano, a vast high plateau at 3,500–4,000m, ringed by snow-capped peaks, with Lake Titicaca and the world's largest salt flat, the Salar de Uyuni, and volcanoes in the southwest.
nature.climate_signature: Cold, dry and intensely sunny at altitude with thin air, a stark, wide-open look — in the rainy season a thin film of water turns the salt flat into a mirror.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Crowded minibuses (micros) and cable-car gondolas linking La Paz and El Alto; 4x4 Toyotas ferry tourists across the salt flats.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good coverage around La Paz and the main highways; limited coverage in remote areas such as Sajama National Park.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same Altiplano, Lake Titicaca shoreline, Quechua and Aymara culture and striped mountain guardrails
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Peru's guardrail stripe has a black outer edge versus a yellow one here; tuktuks and the black-and-white striped sign poles are Peruvian; thick lumber poles and cholets point here.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same high plateau, salt flats and volcanoes across the border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Chile's yellow-reflector bollards and Argentina's chevrons and black Gen 3 car are missing; white-backed Street View car and unpainted lumber poles are found here.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same national road furniture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The west is cold, treeless and mountainous; the east is flat, green and forested.
